formalObservation.Composition:
The composition occupies most of the vertical field and is organized as a stacked sequence of overlapping forms.

Distinct visual units include:

- elongated curved form in upper-left
- rectangular/vertical figure in upper-right
- large rounded figure in middle-left
- large elongated form extending toward middle-right
- small central figure
- large pair of rounded forms in lower portion

The individual forms overlap extensively.
formalObservation.Primary Forms:
- Upper-left curved form
- Upper-right rectangular figure
- Central rounded figure
- Central-right elongated form
- Small central figure
- Lower paired rounded forms
formalObservation.Visible Anatomical / Figure-like Feature:
Several forms contain recognizable figure-like features:

- circular or oval eye-like marks
- facial profiles
- mouths
- tooth-like triangular marks
- limb-like projections
- rounded body forms

Species or anatomical identities are intentionally not assigned.
formalObservation.Structural Forms:
- Rectangular enclosure at upper right
- Horizontal bars
- Vertical structural elements
- Large rounded forms
- Curved enclosing contours
- Layered overlapping structures
formalObservation.Repeated Forms:
- Circular / oval units
- Eye-like forms
- Horizontal bands
- Parallel hatching
- Rounded bodies
- Curved projections
formalObservation.Mark-Making:
Very extensive directional hatching:

- dense diagonal hatching
- horizontal hatching
- thick contour strokes
- dark filled areas
- repeated short linear marks
- overlapping charcoal passages

Hatching appears both within figures and across the surrounding field.
formalObservation.Visual Density:
Very High

One of the densest compositions encountered in the catalogue so far.
formalObservation.Spatial Strategy:
Stacked / Overlapping / Enclosed

Forms develop vertically through overlap, adjacency, contour interruption and changes in charcoal density.
formalObservation.Figure–Ground Relationship: The boundary between figure and surrounding field is relatively porous. Dense hatching extends around several figures, causing some forms to visually merge into the surrounding charcoal structure.
formalObservation.Formal Language:
- Multiple figure-like units share one compressed field.
- Organic and geometric forms coexist.
- Repetition occurs through circular forms and directional hatching.
- Overlap is a major compositional device.
- Density rather than perspective establishes spatial complexity.
- Lower portion contains a strong cluster of rounded forms.
- Upper and middle sections connect through continuous contour and hatching.
